statutorySection: Section 92C read with Rule 10CA and Section 92CE
successorStatute: Income-tax Act, 2025 (Chapter on International Tax & Transfer Pricing)
title: Computation of Arm's Length Price (ALP), Range Concept and Secondary Adjustments

effectivePeriod.annualReset: Annual transfer pricing study documentation and Form 3CEB certification
effectivePeriod.sunsetNotes: Permanent transfer pricing regime under Chapter X of Income-tax Act, 1961.

plainTextSummary: Under Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961, the arm's length price (ALP) in relation to an international transaction or specified domestic transaction must be calculated using the Most Appropriate Method (MAM): Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP), Resale Price Method (RPM), Cost Plus Method (CPM), Profit Split Method (PSM), Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM), or any other method prescribed under Rule 10AB. Under Rule 10CA (introduced by CBDT Notification No. 86/2015), where the dataset of comparable uncontrolled prices contains 6 or more entries, the 'range concept' applies: an arm's length range is constructed from the 35th percentile to the 65th percentile of the sorted dataset. If the transfer price falls within this 35th–65th percentile range, the transaction value is deemed to be at arm's length. If the transaction price falls outside the range, the arm's length price is determined as the 50th percentile (median) of the dataset, and an upward primary transfer pricing adjustment is made. If the dataset has fewer than 6 comparables, the arithmetic mean applies, with a statutory tolerance band (1% for wholesale traders, 3% for all other businesses). Under Section 92CE, where a primary adjustment exceeds ₹1 Crore (₹10,000,000) and is accepted by the assessee or determined in assessment, the excess money must be repatriated to India within 90 days, failing which secondary adjustment interest applies or an additional tax of 18% (plus 12% surcharge and 4% cess, total 20.9664%) is chargeable under Section 92CE(2A).

requiredDocumentChecklist: Form 3CEB Chartered Accountant certification under Section 92E filed before due date
Transfer Pricing Local File documentation containing functional, assets, and risk (FAR) analysis
Master File documentation in Form 3CEAA (where consolidated group turnover and transaction thresholds are met)
Country-by-Country Report (CbCR) in Form 3CEAD for international groups with consolidated revenue exceeding ₹6,400 Crore
Comparable benchmark search process logs with inclusion and rejection matrices
Inter-company agreement / Master Services Agreement (MSA) with Associated Enterprise (AE)
Proof of repatriation within 90 days where primary adjustment exceeds ₹1 Crore under Section 92CE
